Unlike prior segmentation-based methods that require semantic class priors or heuristic-only methods that miss low-frequency static details, HuGS fuses Structure-from-Motion (SfM) features (high-frequency textures) and color residuals from a partially trained NeRF (low-frequency textures) to guide SAM in generating precise static masks [S1].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that HuGS combines 'Structure-from-Motion (SfM)-based heuristics' (which identify static objects characterized by 'high-frequency texture patterns') and 'color residual heuristics derived from a partially trained Nerfacto' (which excel at detecting static elements marked by 'low-frequency textures'). It further explains that these heuristics are used to guide the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to generate static maps. Additionally, the source contrasts this approach with prior methods, noting that segmentation-based methods often require prior knowledge (semantic classes) and that heuristic-only methods can ignore high-frequency details, whereas HuGS addresses these limitations.
